clue.text: Thought Lab team blue? Exactly the opposite

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour; exactly the opposite party is the Conservatives, abbreviated CON
a team is one side in a game
blue is the Conservative colour; exactly the opposite is Labour's red

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a Labour team supporting the blue side, then retracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exactly the opposite' tells you to swap the political words: Lab (Labour) becomes CON (Conservative) and blue (Tory colour) becomes RED (Labour colour), while team stays as SIDE. In Britain blue is the Conservative colour and red the Labour one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mulled over carefully, as in a considered opinion, has been thought through.

clue.text: Best to make a choice, one mother's supporting

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits beneath the others, so mother comes last

parts.note: to opt is to make a choice
one is the Roman numeral I
mum is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Advice that choosing well is best, with a mother's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or ideal outcome, the top option.

clue.text: Sandown doesn't have its own beach?

indicators.note: not having something means those letters are taken out of the racecourse name

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether the seaside town of Sandown lacks a beach of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandown is a resort on the Isle of Wight (and a racecourse); 'its' just refers back to Sandown. The question mark marks the definition as an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach is made of fine grains on the shore, so the shore material stands for the whole beach.

clue.text: Head of chapter restricts company for church officer

indicators.note: to restrict is to confine, so the head of chapter encloses the company

parts.note: a dean presides over a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A senior cleric keeps tight control over who mixes with church officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of chapter' looks like a first-letter instruction (C), but it is the dean who heads a cathedral chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: In many churches this is an ordained minister or lay officer below a priest.

clue.text: Contradiction's genuine about object of ridicule

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for genuine goes round the target of mockery

parts.note: real means genuine
the butt of a joke is its object of ridicule

explanation.surface: A sincere denial concerning someone who is being mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a counterargument that refutes a claim, so it contradicts it.

clue.text: Speak slowly, line getting to drag on

indicators.note: getting to means arriving at, so the line letter joins the end of the drag

parts.note: to draw on a cigarette is to drag on it, so drag means draw

explanation.surface: Someone talks slowly, the queue of words dragging on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy, slow manner of speech with drawn-out vowels; as a verb it means speaking that way.

clue.text: Miser keeping pile in curious casket

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the reworked casket holds the pile
curious means odd or strange, signalling the letters of casket rearranged

parts.note: a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A miser hoards a heap of treasure in an odd chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curious' is the anagram signal and 'keeping' the containment one; the pile sits after the first letter of the rearranged casket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who hates spending, just like a miser.

clue.text: Plant is favourite — any number I planted in middle of quad

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: planted in means set inside, so these letters go into the central part of quad
the middle of a word is its central letters, here the two inside quad

parts.note: N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: A gardener's favourite flower has been planted in the middle of a college quad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of quad' gives UA, and 'planted in' puts N and I between U and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a popular garden flower with trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Aptly learn swimming, as father treats child?

indicators.note: letters that are swimming are moving around, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child learns to swim, as a father would teach them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges APTLY and LEARN together; the definition with its question mark describes how a dad behaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a fatherly way is the manner in which a dad deals with his offspring.

clue.text: Supporters rush finally forward

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so take the closing letter of rush

explanation.surface: Fans charge forward in a last-minute surge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporters' looks like fans but means bras.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward here is an adjective for someone bold or pushy, the same as being impudently bold.

clue.text: Burial place of Thomas Black

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Where someone called Thomas Black lies buried.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomb is a vault or grave for interring the dead.

clue.text: Omelette's wrong — one sent back everything

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A complaint that the omelette is wrong, so it is all sent back to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish tortilla is a thick egg and potato dish, a type of omelette.

clue.text: Project finished, needing change in the middle

parts.note: over means finished or ended

indicators.note: in the middle means the inner letters, so take change without its ends

explanation.surface: A project is complete but needs some alteration midway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb meaning to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to jut out beyond something, as a ledge or roof does over a wall.

clue.text: Get rid of me over anagramming

indicators.note: anagramming openly announces that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to stop someone forever making anagrams of their name.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove something is to take it away or eliminate it.

clue.text: Plain girl father initially supported

parts.note: Pam is a girl's name
pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the opening letter of supported

explanation.surface: A plain-looking girl whose father backed her at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' looks like an adjective describing the girl, but it is a noun for flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are vast treeless grassland plains of South America.

clue.text: Potential seafront walk is ending in Hove

parts.note: prom is short for promenade, a seafront walkway

indicators.note: ending in means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The seaside promenade at Hove shows potential.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town next to Brighton on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone showing promise has potential, the capacity to develop and succeed.

clue.text: Like a word, however Balzac uses it

indicators.note: uses means the phrase holds the answer within its letters, spanning both words

explanation.surface: A wordsmith remarks on how the novelist Balzac uses a particular word.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbal means relating to or consisting of words.

clue.text: Bad robes altered and taken up

indicators.note: altered means changed, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Badly made robes are altered by a tailor and their hems taken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' looks like tailoring, but it means engrossed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken up with something means being engrossed or fully occupied by it.

clue.text: Small whip cut

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothes sizes
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: A short whip that has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To slash is to cut with a sweeping stroke, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Roman garment of past time on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means returning, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman robe from a bygone era is making a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose draped outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Swindle involving current 50p, say

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the swindle wraps round the current

parts.note: a con is a swindle
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A scam involving fifty pence in loose change.
explanation.walkthrough: A 50p is a British fifty-pence piece; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifty-pence piece is an example of a metal currency piece.

clue.text: American transporter hit in Los Angeles

indicators.note: in means inside, so the strike goes within the city's abbreviation

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A vehicle from the USA is struck in a collision in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American transporter' suggests a car or truck, but it is the South American pack animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal used to carry loads, so a beast of burden from the Americas.

clue.text: Element some uncovered in salty water

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the central letters go into the salty water

parts.note: brine is salty water

indicators.note: uncovered means with its outer letters stripped off, leaving the inside of some

explanation.surface: A chemical element is found in seawater.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromine is a chemical element, a reddish-brown liquid halogen extracted from seawater.

clue.text: Drunk left together with Queen is northern Scot

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
and means together with
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A drunk wanders off with the Queen, who turns out to be a Scot from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Highlands, the mountainous north of Scotland.
